target_customer: Engineering teams running apps on their own AWS account (startups and growth stage), and their AI agents
problem: Heroku is limiting and expensive while AWS is complex; teams want a Heroku or Vercel like deploy experience inside their own AWS account.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for CI/CD, deploys and Terraform automation in the customer's AWS account

founders.name: Brandon Bayer
previous_startups: Blitz.js (open source framework creator, per YC page and Ravion site)
founders.background_notes: Podcast and interview pages say he studied electrical engineering and worked as a software engineer; no employer named in a source opened.

founders.name: Mina Abadir
founders.background_notes: Ravion site says deep AWS and infrastructure consulting experience; no employer named.

competitors.name: Heroku
competitors.what: Platform as a service that Flightcontrol positioned against as too limiting and expensive
competitors.traction_then: Incumbent PaaS with large developer base

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating builds, deploys and infrastructure inside a customer's AWS account across ECS, EC2 and RDS needs deep AWS knowledge but is standard engineering for a small team. The Ravion launch post says it took 13 months to rebuild.

defensibility.rationale: Deep deployment integration creates some switching costs, but rivals such as Render, Railway and Terraform Cloud offered alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents absorbing the wedge; the team says Flightcontrol reached profitability and rebuilt it as Ravion.

market_need_then: The Flightcontrol pitch cites the migration away from Heroku due to cost and limits; the CEO's open source Blitz.js community gave a developer audience.

branding.domain_note: ravion.com is the exact word domain; Flightcontrol used flightcontrol.dev.

identity.visual_style: developer tool site modeled on Vercel style
identity.voice_and_tone: Speed, safety and no lock-in; software factory for teams and agents

rebrands.why: Ravion presented as the next generation successor of Flightcontrol per the company site; date and reason not given

branding.community_and_virality: CEO is creator of Blitz.js and has appeared on developer podcasts such as Syntax and PodRocket

brand_strength.rationale: Flightcontrol had developer podcast exposure, but the new name has little independent press; strength is hard to judge.

pivots.to: Ravion, AWS platform for agents and humans with Terraform
pivots.why: Company says Ravion is the successor built over 13 months; date not stated

outcome_analysis: The YC W22 company was Flightcontrol, a deployment layer on customers' AWS accounts built by the creator of Blitz.js. The company says it ran in production since 2021 and reached profitability, then rebuilt the product as Ravion for the agent era. Funding is not reliably documented, so the record shows a small, apparently capital efficient team with an unclear financing history.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights about $500K across 5 rounds, Extruct $125K seed, PitchBook $2.12M total, Caplight lists Global Founders Capital, Cervin Ventures, YC, Soma Capital and others as seed investors. All aggregators with conflicting totals, so no rounds recorded. Competitor sources are undated vendor pages; Render and Railway are listed by AlternativeTo but undated. The YC directory entry for Ravion shows the batch as Winter 2022 but the company was Flightcontrol then.
